correctness.rationale: Explicit index-three coset construction sends a partial transversal of H to disjoint zero-sum triples of G; Goddyn--Halasz Theorem 2 supplies size m-1. The remaining three points take at most two rational lines. Bézout plus sum(G)=unique involution rules out m-line perfect covering. Hall--Paige full mapping (Goddyn--Halasz Theorem 4) or Cichacz recovers m in the complementary 2-torsion cases. Exact cyclic finite checks are supplementary only.

value.rationale: The originating source poses the exact minimum finite-field line-cover problem. A unique rational involution is a natural, sharp obstruction class not resolved by zero-sum perfect-packing literature. The theorem determines the minimum for every such smooth flex-marked cubic when 3 divides its rational point count, with an unavoidable and sufficient error of exactly one independent of field size, making the transition from combinatorial existence to exact geometric optimum substantive despite its concise proof.
